data.description:
Discovered while landing Gerrit change 1640 for ticket sole-curbable-stinkpot (9a71-ba9b-89d0-4cb8). It cost that change a spurious Verified -1.

TEST: tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py::test_cli_keyset_is_informational_and_keeps_json_envelope_read_only

OBSERVED: CI run 31571454820, leg 'pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)'. 1 failed, 12134 passed — every other matrix leg green. The assertion diff is a SINGLE stray entry:

    Right contains 1 more item:
    {'.git/objects/maintenance.lock': b''}

MECHANISM: the test asserts byte-for-byte equality of the tracker directory before and after a read-only 'bridge fsck --keyset' invocation:

    full_before = _file_bytes(full_tracker)      # line 201
    keyset_before = _file_bytes(keyset_tracker)  # line 202
    ...
    assert _file_bytes(full_tracker) == full_before      # line 222
    assert _file_bytes(keyset_tracker) == keyset_before  # line 223

_file_bytes (line 162) walks the WHOLE directory, '.git/' included, with no exclusion for transient git internals. Git background auto-maintenance creates and releases '.git/objects/maintenance.lock' asynchronously, so if it exists at snapshot time and is gone by assert time (or vice versa) the comparison flips. Nothing about the command under test changed the store — the read-only property the test is actually asserting still holds.

The intent of the test is sound: prove the keyset path does not mutate the store. The bug is that the oracle over-reaches into git's own scratch state.

SUGGESTED FIX (pick one):
- Have _file_bytes ignore transient git internals (*.lock under .git/, .git/objects/maintenance.lock, .git/gc.pid) — narrowest change, keeps the read-only assertion meaningful for the store files that matter.
- Or restrict the snapshot to the store payload (.bridge_state/ + event files) and drop .git/ entirely, since git plumbing state is not what 'read-only' is claiming.
- Or disable auto-maintenance in the fixture (git config maintenance.auto false, gc.auto 0) — fixes this repo but leaves the oracle fragile to the next transient file.

Prefer the first or second: disabling maintenance only hides the class.

Passes locally on macOS (3 passed), so it is genuinely intermittent, not deterministic.
data.title: Flaky: bridge fsck keyset read-only test races git auto-maintenance on macOS
